# Blocks by need

<!-- Generated by `node tools/blocks/build-catalog.mjs` from blocks/catalog.json. Don't edit by hand: change the
     block.json (or the catalogue entry) and run the script again. -->

Every block in the kit, grouped by what the player does or what the game needs. A block can be under two headings.
65 blocks: 28 Meticulai blocks (systems from games on meticulai.com, each links to its game)
and 37 from Patch and other authors. Details and licences: `blocks/catalog.json` and
`blocks/README.md`.

For your own game, let the kit point you: `node tools/blocks/suggest.mjs` reads `my-game/GREAT.md` and lists the
blocks whose "use when" matches it, with the words that matched. Add one with `node tools/blocks/add.mjs <id>`.

"Works with the starter" means it runs with the starter's normal renderer. "Needs WebGPU" means switching the game to
three.js's WebGPU renderer (a real job; see `blocks/README.md`, "Check the renderer").

## You fly or glide

- **Arcade flight (mouse aim)** (`meticulai-arcade-flight`): The flight model, mouse-aim piloting and chase camera of a live dogfighting game. The flyer goes where its nose points with a little slip, dives for speed and pays for...
  Use when the player flies a creature, plane or glider in third person and should steer by pointing the mouse, with speed, energy, boost and stall mattering, or bots must fly the same way as players.
  From Dragon Aces ([play it](https://meticulai.com/games/dragon-aces/)), tuned by playing. No renderer needed; ready.
- **Glider flight (lift, stall, thermals)** (`meticulai-glider-flight`): A hang glider's flight model: the pilot sets angle of attack and bank, lift grows with airspeed squared, drag has parasitic and induced parts, the wing stalls when slow...
  Use when the player flies, glides or soars without an engine (hang glider, paraglider, bird, wingsuit, paper plane, kite) and height for speed, lift, stall, finding rising air and landing should matter.
  From Hezarfen, Kite Race ([play it](https://meticulai.com/games/hezarfen/)), tuned by playing. No renderer needed; ready.

## You ride or drive

- **Horse locomotion law (no sliding, real turns) with a movement checker** (`meticulai-horse-locomotion`): One movement law for every horse: bounded acceleration and braking, turns limited by speed (no pivoting at rest, wide arcs at a gallop), motion only along the facing...
  Use when the game has horses, riders, deer, camels or any four-legged or wheeled body that must move believably (no strafing, no moonwalking, no spinning on the spot), especially many of them, and you want a...
  From TUMEN (not on the site yet), tuned by playing. No renderer needed; ready.
- **Realistic car** (`car`): A car on Rapier at real scale and gravity: tyres that build grip, peak and let go, visible suspension, engine and gearbox, handbrake, and tarmac, gravel and grass.
  Good for: Driving, rally and delivery games that should feel physical; a car to drop into an open world.
  By Patch (patch.gg). Works with the starter; ready.

## You shoot, throw or aim

- **Archery aim** (`meticulai-archery-aim`): Bow shooting that feels fair from a moving mount: hold to draw, let go, and the arrow goes where the crosshair was.
  Use when the player shoots arrows, spears, thrown objects or other slow projectiles, especially from a moving horse, vehicle or boat at moving targets, and aiming should feel immediate and fair, or the scene...
  From TUMEN (not on the site yet), tuned by playing. Works with the starter; ready.
- **00GameDevs magic VFX starter pack** (`00gamedevs-vfx`): Five magic effects by their author (Darkchain Sigil Rupture, Rift-Shattering Slashes, Luminous Vortex Black Hole, Golden Chain Rain, Sacred Relic Descent), one ES module...
  Good for: Big flashy magic moments in a three.js game; the author's site has a larger free catalog with an agent integration guide.
  By 00GameDevs (00vchannel). Works with the starter; pointed to (downloaded from the author).
- **Elemental Sandbox (October): cinematic spells and ragdolls** (`cinematic-spells`): Five 6 to 12 second spell set pieces that act on real bodies: chains, lightning, roots, crystals and falling planets pin, tear and slice ragdolls (its own position-based...
  Good for: Finishers, boss moves, spectacle moments in a magic game.
  By mohamedachrefelouafi (Chiro Visuals). Works with the starter; pointed to (downloaded from the author).
- **Elemental Sandbox abilities (August and September)** (`elemental-abilities`): Character abilities with ground aim indicators, decals, lights, particles and camera shake: Frost Lance, Storm Lance, Cinder Fall, Nova Beam, Voltaic Snare, Glacial...
  Good for: Action RPGs, MOBA-style or top-down casters that need aimed abilities.
  By mohamedachrefelouafi (Chiro Visuals). Works with the starter; pointed to (downloaded from the author).
- **Ultra Elements (spell VFX)** (`ultra-elements`): 39 real-time elemental spells (fire, ice, lightning, wind, water, earth, void, light, acid, arcane), each simulated on the GPU and tunable.
  Good for: Magic, wizard and action games that need big readable spells.
  By Humpalumps. Works with the starter; pointed to (downloaded from the author).

## Crowds, herds, flocks

- **Firefly swarm** (`meticulai-firefly-swarm`): Catchable fireflies that wander in a loose flock, blink on their own rhythms, drift toward a still open hand, scatter from a fast snatch, glow inside a closed fist and...
  Use when a calm game needs glowing creatures or particles that react to the player (fireflies, wisps, spirits, sparks, plankton) and must glow softly without blown-out bloom, especially a catch-gently mechanic.
  From Fireflies ([play it](https://meticulai.com/games/show-of-hands/)), tuned by playing. Works with the starter; ready.
- **Flock (murmuration)** (`meticulai-flock`): Thousands of boids on the CPU with a counting-sort spatial hash, steered as one cloud: attraction to a player-set target around a hollow core, a coherent swirl field so...
  Use when the game has flocks, swarms or schools (birds, bats, fish, insects), or the player controls a crowd as one body.
  From Murmur (not on the site yet). Works with the starter; ready.
- **Crowds and navigation** (`crowds`): Make enemies and crowds walk around any three.js level: build a navmesh from its meshes, spawn people, give them a goal.
  Good for: Enemies that chase, townsfolk, armies, herds, tower-defence paths; any game where many characters must find their way.
  By Patch (patch.gg), on recast-navigation-js by Isaac Mason. Works with the starter; ready.
- **recast-navigation-js (navmesh and crowds)** (`recast-navigation`): Navmesh building, pathfinding and crowd simulation in the browser, with three.js helpers (@recast-navigation/three).
  Good for: Any game where characters must find their way around a 3D level.
  By Isaac Mason (WebAssembly port of Recast and Detour by Mikko Mononen, Zlib). No renderer needed; pointed to (downloaded from the author).

## Water, sky, weather

  Use when an outdoor three.js world should feel big and atmospheric (valleys, coasts, cities, flying or open-world games), with far things fading into the sky instead of a hard fog wall or clear air.
  From Hezarfen ([play it](https://meticulai.com/games/hezarfen/)). Works with the starter; ready.

- **Sonar sketch** (`meticulai-sonar-sketch`): A sonar ping that draws the world: 900 rays march outward with the expanding front through any distance/density field and leave glowing points on the walls the moment...
  Use when the player navigates darkness, fog or an unseen space by echolocation, radar, scanner pulses or a reveal wave, and the level can be described by a distance or density function.
  From Abyssal (not on the site yet). Works with the starter; ready.
- **Fire** (`fire`): Real 3D flames made only in shader math (a ray-marched volume): candle, torch, gas jet, campfire, brazier, fireplace, bonfire, burning crate, fire line, with sparks...
  Good for: Any game with fire you can walk around and lean into: camps, torches, braziers, burning props.
  By Patch (patch.gg). Works with the starter; ready.
- **Grass you can touch** (`touch-grass`): A meadow to the horizon that reacts and remembers: grass bends under feet and anything rolling on it, a scythe mows it and lays the stems in rows, fire spreads with the...

- **Eanpa Sky (stylised sky)** (`eanpa-sky`): A volumetric sky and weather engine for three.js WebGPU (TSL): soft painted-looking cumulus, time of day, morphing weather, cloud shadows.
  Good for: Outdoor games with a soft, painterly sky and changing weather.
  By SkyeShark. Needs WebGPU; pointed to (downloaded from the author).
- **Effekseer for WebGL (+ CC0 sample effects)** (`effekseer`): Plays particle effects made in the free Effekseer editor inside three.js. The editor ships stylised fantasy sample effects (fire, water, lightning, slashes, heals...
  Good for: Stylised fantasy combat effects made by effect artists; teams that want to author effects in an editor.

- **ProceduralTerrains** (`procedural-terrains`): Whole worlds from a seed: volcanic coasts, islands, snowy peaks, canyons, dunes, with water, clouds, erosion and an infinite or planet mode.
  Good for: Flying, strategy, island and far-away land seen from the air.
  By ZyFou. Works with the starter; pointed to (downloaded from the author).
- **Ultra Elements (spell VFX)** (`ultra-elements`): 39 real-time elemental spells (fire, ice, lightning, wind, water, earth, void, light, acid, arcane), each simulated on the GPU and tunable.

- **Ultra-Water (ocean)** (`ultra-water`): A real-time FFT ocean: shore breakers, foam, caustics, an underwater view with sun shafts, a sky with clouds.

  By Humpalumps. Works with the starter; pointed to (downloaded from the author).
- **webgpu-skyscape (volumetric clouds and atmosphere)** (`skyscape-clouds`): Real volumetric clouds with cloud shadows and light shafts, a day-night cycle with sun, moon and stars, and aerial haze.
  Good for: Flight games and big realistic outdoor skies.
  By nagoya0, porting takram's three-clouds and three-atmosphere (Shota Matsuda). Needs WebGPU; pointed to (downloaded from the author).

  By blendi for Patch (patch.gg). Works with the starter; ready.

  By blendi for Patch (patch.gg). Works with the starter; ready.

  Good for: Bright, hopeful, hand-painted outdoor games; walking, gliding, farming or adventure games set outdoors.
  By blendi for Patch (patch.gg). Works with the starter; ready.
- **Patchwork quilt** (`patchwork-quilt`): Makes a world out of cloth: a quilt of puffed patches with real seams and stitches, fuzzy felt, and a tilt-shift camera that sees it as a small thing on a table.
  Good for: Toy-like, handmade, miniature looks; cosy and family games; stop-motion feel.
  By blendi for Patch (patch.gg). Works with the starter; ready.
- **pixelfx (pixel art effects)** (`pixelfx`): 244 pixel art effects, each a small piece of code drawing into a low-resolution frame: fire, explosions, magic, hits, weather, pickups, UI, critters, and 12 whole...
  Good for: Pixel art and retro games (canvas, Phaser, PixiJS, Kaplay); pixel-style effects on a three.js game via a CanvasTexture or an overlay canvas.
  By Patch (patch.gg). 2D canvas; ready.
- **Watercolour** (`watercolour`): A world that starts as a pencil drawing and is painted in watercolour as you walk through it: the wash spreads from your feet, climbs the trees and stays.
  Good for: Gentle exploration games where the player "colours in" the world; storybook looks; a reveal mechanic built into the look.
  By blendi for Patch (patch.gg). Works with the starter; ready.
- **Pixel Plays (isometric pixel dioramas)** (`pixel-plays`): Small browser games as isometric pixel dioramas: describe a ground, place boxes, spheres, trees and people, and get hue-shifted light, dither, hard shadows and wind.
  Good for: Cosy isometric pixel games; tiny sports or puzzle games; a distinct pixel look without sprites.
  By Amir Mushich (concept by abhi). 2D canvas; pointed to (downloaded from the author).
- **trompe (paint a grey level with image models)** (`trompe`): Textures a whole grey blockout level with image models: plans cameras where a player can stand, paints what each sees, projects and bakes one texture lit by a real sun...
  Good for: Realistic buildings seen from a few metres or more; trailers; a first look at a level before real art.
  By Patch (patch.gg). No renderer needed; pointed to (downloaded from the author).

## Hands, face and webcam controls

- **Blink input (webcam eyes and look-away)** (`meticulai-blink-input`): Turns the webcam into a controller: eyes closed (both eyes to close, either eye to open, so squints and winks never count), looking away (head turned, face out of frame...
  Use when the game is played with the player's eyes or face: blinking, closing the eyes, looking away from the screen or turning the head (for example 'it only moves when you can't see it').
  From Don't Blink ([play it](https://meticulai.com/games/dont-blink/)). No renderer needed; ready.
- **Hand controls (webcam gestures)** (`meticulai-hand-controls`): Play with bare hands in front of a webcam. One call opens the camera and runs Google's MediaPipe hand tracker in the browser (GPU with CPU fallback), mirrors it like a...
  Use when the player controls the game with their bare hands through a webcam: pointing, pinching, making a fist, swiping, throwing or clapping.
  From Show of Hands (the 14 hands games), GODHAND ([play it](https://meticulai.com/games/show-of-hands/)), tuned by playing. No renderer needed; ready.

## Music and sound

- **Adaptive music** (`meticulai-adaptive-music`): A whole adaptive soundtrack synthesised live with Web Audio, no files: electric piano, synth bass, clav, a sax-like lead, strings, vibes and a jazz kit with reverb...
  Use when the game wants music that reacts to speed, danger or progress without shipping audio files or paying for generated tracks.
  From Last Drop ([play it](https://meticulai.com/games/last-drop/)). No renderer needed; ready.
- **Procedural songs** (`meticulai-procedural-songs`): Whole songs from a seed with no sound files: a hook melody over 4-bar chord progressions, drums, bass, arpeggio, pad and lead synthesised with Web Audio.
  Use when the game wants background music that never repeats and rises with tension or game phase, without audio files or paid generated tracks.
  From Deadweight (not on the site yet). No renderer needed; ready.

## Physics and simulation

- **Marble physics** (`meticulai-marble-physics`): Deterministic sphere physics for marbles and balls at 60 Hz with 4 substeps: oriented boxes, cylinders, lathe shells (bowls, funnels, banked turns) and helix shells...
  Use when the game rolls balls or marbles over a built track or table and wants physics that feels like a toy and is deterministic enough for replays, share links, bots or multiplayer.
  From Lost Marbles ([play it](https://meticulai.com/games/lost-marbles/)), tuned by playing. No renderer needed; ready.
- **Rope and cloth chains** (`meticulai-rope-cloth-chains`): Short verlet chains pinned at one end to a moving point and simulated in world space, so scarves, ribbons, hair, sashes, tails, banners and short ropes trail every...
  Use when a character, creature, vehicle or prop needs follow-through (scarf, cape tails, hair, ribbons, tail, antennae, banner, a dangling rope) that trails its movement without hand animation.
  From Inkbound (not on the site yet). No renderer needed; ready.
- **Sand trails** (`meticulai-sand-trails`): Soft ground that remembers, simulated on the GPU in a small square that follows a moving body: a groove with berms and a bow wave, craters with rims on landing, water...
  Use when something moves over a soft surface (sand, snow, mud, wet ground) and should leave a trail, groove, crater or footprints that fade.
  From Last Drop ([play it](https://meticulai.com/games/last-drop/)), tuned by playing. Works with the starter; ready.
- **Destruction physics** (`destruction`): Breakable structures on the GPU: a timber barn, a steel water tower, a brick wall and a chimney, each hundreds of rigid pieces welded together, knocked down piece by...
  Good for: Demolition, siege and catapult games; physics sandboxes; big satisfying collapses.
  By Patch (patch.gg), on three-avbd by Steven Bobyn. Needs WebGPU; ready.
- **Slice anything** (`slice-anything`): Cut any mesh along any plane, as many times as you like: every piece becomes a closed solid with its own Rapier body, and the cut face shows what the thing is made of...
  Good for: Sword, knife and slicing games; satisfying destruction of props; physics toys.
  By blendi for Patch (patch.gg). WebGPU, falls back to WebGL 2; ready.
- **Soil Studio (GrassSystemThreeJS)** (`soil-and-grass`): Shader soil with mounds, moss, cracks and damp patches under about 200,000 wind-blown grass blades in one draw, with volumetric mist.
  Good for: A beautiful patch of ground: gardens, farms, small outdoor arenas.
  By mohamedachrefelouafi (Chiro Visuals). Works with the starter; pointed to (downloaded from the author).
- **three-avbd (GPU rigid-body physics)** (`three-avbd`): Augmented Vertex Block Descent (SIGGRAPH 2025) rigid bodies solved in WebGPU compute shaders, with breakable joints. The physics under the destruction block.
  Good for: Thousands of stacked or jointed bodies on the GPU.
  By Steven Bobyn. Needs WebGPU; pointed to (downloaded from the author).
- **three-voxel-destruction** (`voxel-destruction`): Teardown-style voxel destruction on the GPU: buildings of thousands of voxel bodies that really fall when what holds them up is knocked out.
  Good for: Voxel demolition and siege games.
  By Steven Bobyn. Needs WebGPU; pointed to (downloaded from the author).
- **Three.js Particle Fluids** (`particle-fluids`): Liquid, jelly, cloth and smoke as GPU particles (position-based fluids in WebGPU compute shaders); liquid, jelly and cloth push on each other.
  Good for: Pouring, sloshing, gooey or cloth toys; a liquid puzzle; a showpiece effect.
  By Daniel Greenheck. Needs WebGPU; pointed to (downloaded from the author).

- **Lowpoly Tree Generator** (`lowpoly-tree-generator`): Faceted low-poly trees from six archetypes (about 1,500 triangles, vertex colours, no textures), rigged so a tree can walk, jump, stomp and swing.
  Good for: Low-poly stylised worlds; a tree character; quick forests that match Kenney-style assets.
  By Pajama Studio (Rand Monster contributors). Works with the starter; pointed to (downloaded from the author).
- **procedural-animals** (`procedural-animals`): 24 real animals built, rigged and furred entirely in code: createAnimal('wolf'), add it to the scene and steer it.
  Good for: Wildlife, hunting, herding, safari or farm games; creatures without any model files.
  By Majid Manzarpour and contributors. Works with the starter; pointed to (downloaded from the author).
- **Soil Studio (GrassSystemThreeJS)** (`soil-and-grass`): Shader soil with mounds, moss, cracks and damp patches under about 200,000 wind-blown grass blades in one draw, with volumetric mist.
  Good for: A beautiful patch of ground: gardens, farms, small outdoor arenas.
  By mohamedachrefelouafi (Chiro Visuals). Works with the starter; pointed to (downloaded from the author).
- **three-voxel-destruction** (`voxel-destruction`): Teardown-style voxel destruction on the GPU: buildings of thousands of voxel bodies that really fall when what holds them up is knocked out.
  Good for: Voxel demolition and siege games.
  By Steven Bobyn. Needs WebGPU; pointed to (downloaded from the author).
- **threejs-nanites (forests at scale)** (`nanite-forests`): A WebGPU renderer that draws any tree a million times: culling, impostors, wind, shadows, temporal upscaling and an auto-quality budget, with forest floor, grass, sky...
  Good for: Huge forests and open worlds in a WebGPU game.
  By Victor Zakharov. Needs WebGPU; pointed to (downloaded from the author).

## Tuning and testing

- **Tuning panel** (`meticulai-tuning-panel`): A side panel of live sliders, switches, choices and colours for every feel number in the game, with the game's own value beside each, changed values marked in gold...
  Use when a person will tune the game's feel by playing it and should hand the exact numbers back to the agent instead of describing them.
  From TUMEN, Hezarfen, Inkbound, Scrapfall, Still Life 2 ([play it](https://meticulai.com/games/hezarfen/)), tuned by playing. No renderer needed; ready.

## Everything else (characters, cameras, menus, game rules)

- **Anim springs (springs, inertialization, layers, IK)** (`meticulai-anim-springs`): A three.js animation toolkit: exact critically damped and bouncy springs (frame-rate independent), inertialized transitions with no pops, a layer stack (base plus...
  Use when characters, creatures, hands, cameras or props should move smoothly and alive (follow, reach, look, breathe, switch moves) without hand-made animation files or visible pops.
  From Bonesworth ([play it](https://meticulai.com/games/bonesworth/)). No renderer needed; ready.
- **Crowd renderer: thousands of animated riders and animals** (`meticulai-crowd-renderer`): Draws thousands of animated, skinned horses and riders (or any rigged model: herds, flocks, people) in a few draw calls.
  Use when the game needs hundreds or thousands of animated characters, animals or mounted riders on screen at once (armies, cavalry, herds, crowds, flocks) at 60 fps in the browser.
  From TUMEN (not on the site yet). Works with the starter; ready.
- **Deterministic math** (`meticulai-deterministic-math`): A drop-in replacement for Math whose sin, cos, tan, atan, atan2, asin, acos, exp, log, pow and hypot are fdlibm ports built only from + - * / and sqrt, so a simulation...
  Use when a simulation is re-run from its inputs somewhere else and must come out identical: replays or ghosts stored as inputs, share links, lockstep multiplayer, server-checked scores, bots or level solvers...
  From Lost Marbles: Trick Shot ([play it](https://meticulai.com/games/trick-shot/)). No renderer needed; ready.
- **Impossible spaces (portals)** (`impossible-spaces`): Portals: join any two rectangular openings and look, walk and throw through them. Rooms bigger inside than out, loops, a door onto a wall, a door that shrinks you to a...
  Good for: Puzzle and exploration games built on impossible architecture; non-Euclidean levels; surprise moments.
  By blendi for Patch (patch.gg). Needs WebGPU; ready.
- **anymove (motion capture for any creature from one AI video)** (`anymove`): Turns one AI video into a real animation on a creature's own skeleton (wings, tails, eight legs): two cameras in one frame, a DINOv2 joint reader, the rig fitted in both...
  Good for: Custom animations for odd creatures that no animation pack covers.
  By Patch (patch.gg). No renderer needed; pointed to (downloaded from the author).
- **GeometryPainterThreeJS** (`geometry-painter`): Drag across any mesh and geometry grows along the stroke: quartz crystals, molten cracks, aurora silk, a glowing reef. Instanced and animated in shaders.
  Good for: Magic "painting" mechanics, crystal growth, corruption spreading over a surface; level dressing.
  By mohamedachrefelouafi (Chiro Visuals). WebGPU, falls back to WebGL 2; pointed to (downloaded from the author).
